name: Baseline-Flat-v2
why_v2: v1 judged forward speed and survival only, so a policy that drags its head on the floor while shuffling its feet passed all three gates: the same rollout measured forward_mae 0.0199, displacement +9.46 m, survival 1.000, while neck_pitch carried 82-94 N (47-49% of body weight) with its collision mesh 5.2 cm below the floor and one hind foot at 0.002 duty.

The quantities needed were already pinned elsewhere in this repo, and the v1 protocol simply did not read them: the geometric fall predicate (metrics.fall_flags: tilt <= 40 deg or clearance below threshold, sustained), the v10 DIAGNOSE.md non-foot carrier criterion (chest/neck normal force > 10% of body weight sustained > 0.5 s), and the collision-mesh reading that separates 'resting on' from 'through the floor'.

Every threshold below is therefore a repo precedent, not a new opinion. The pre-train probe (rl_exp/tools/verify/baseline_probe.py) measures the same quantities through the same functions (rl_exp/tools/diagnose/diag_metrics.py), so a standard set before training is re-measured at acceptance instead of being replaced by a weaker one.
